title: Find a tote location by typing the tote number in the container section (jump to tote’s map location)
summary: Use the RMS map’s container section tote lookup to enter a tote number and navigate the map to the tote’s current location in the system.
when_to_use: Use when you know the tote number but need to quickly navigate the RMS map to where that tote is currently represented in the system (for example, to recover from an incorrect tote being on the wrong location).
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Execute the RMS container section tote lookup by tote number and verify the map navigates to the tote’s current location.
access_or_tools_needed: Tote number input/search in the container section

access_required: Access to the Geek+ RMS web application/map view that includes the container section tote lookup.
system_preconditions: The tote number you enter must be the tote’s identifier as shown/used in the RMS map.

visual_references.description: RMS map view showing rack/container selection context and the tote lookup concept (dark blue vs light blue racks; typing tote number in container section to jump to tote location).

steps.title: Open the container section in the RMS/map view
steps.purpose: Get to the RMS container section that supports tote lookup by tote number.
steps.instruction: In the Geek+ RMS web map view, open/select the container section so you can use the tote number search/input.
steps.expected_result: The container section is visible and ready for tote number entry/search.
steps.healthy_condition: You can see the container section UI area where tote lookup is performed.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot access the container section UI or there is no tote number input/search available.

actions.label: Open container section
actions.exact_action: Open the container section in the RMS/map view.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “To look at more information about the rack, you have to click on the container selection…”

steps.title: Type the tote number into the container section search/input field
steps.purpose: Trigger the RMS tote lookup by tote number.
steps.instruction: In the container section, type the tote number into the tote search/input field.
steps.expected_result: The tote number is entered into the container section tote lookup field.
steps.healthy_condition: The tote number you entered is present in the container section search/input.
steps.failure_condition: The tote number cannot be entered (field not available) or the entered value is not accepted/does not populate.

actions.label: Enter tote number
actions.exact_action: Type the tote number on this container section

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “You can find a tote by typing the tote number on this container section…”
OCR: “You can also find a tote by typing the … Location 11801070 number in and selecting the rack or AGV … it’s located on if its in the system.”

steps.title: Submit/confirm the tote number so the map navigates to the tote’s location
steps.purpose: Cause RMS to navigate the map to the part of the map where the tote is currently represented.
steps.instruction: Submit/confirm the entered tote number using the container section UI action (as supported by the RMS interface) so the map navigates to the tote’s location.
steps.expected_result: The map view moves to the location where the specified tote number is present in the system.
steps.healthy_condition: After confirmation, the map jumps to the tote’s rack/container area associated with that tote number.
steps.failure_condition: The map does not navigate to the expected tote location for the tote number entered.

actions.label: Confirm tote lookup
actions.exact_action: Submit/confirm the entry (as supported by the UI) so the map navigates to the part of the map where that tote has been added / wherever that tote is in the system.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the map does not navigate to the expected tote location, stop and escalate for further investigation of tote addition/removal correctness.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “...it will take you to the part of the map where that tote's been added or wherever that tote is in the system.”

steps.title: Identify the tote’s current rack/location from the navigated map view
steps.purpose: Use the navigated map location to determine where the tote currently is for follow-on actions (e.g., swap or remove/re-add).
steps.instruction: From the navigated map location, identify the tote’s current rack/location in the RMS map so you can proceed with the next support action.
steps.expected_result: You can see the tote’s rack/location on the map at the navigated location corresponding to the tote number.
steps.healthy_condition: The rack/container area shown at the navigated location corresponds to the tote number you searched (and the rack shows tote presence vs empty using the map’s rack color indication).
steps.failure_condition: The navigated location does not show the tote as expected (for example, the rack appears empty when you expect the tote to be present).

actions.label: Inspect navigated rack/container
actions.exact_action: Use the navigated map location to identify the tote’s current rack/location

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “There are two distinct color… dark blue… means it has a toad on it… light blue… means it's empty.”
OCR: “Dark blue indicates the presence of a tote. While light blue represents empty rack.”

success_criteria: After confirming the tote number in the container section, the RMS map navigates to the location where that tote is present in the system.
healthy_conditions: The container section tote lookup field accepts the tote number entry.
The map jumps to the tote’s represented location for the entered tote number.
At the navigated rack/container, the rack color indication aligns with tote presence (dark blue for tote present; light blue for empty).
failure_conditions: The map does not navigate to the expected tote location for the entered tote number.
The navigated rack/container appears empty (light blue) when the tote should be present.
escalation_guidance: If the map does not navigate to the expected tote location, stop and escalate for further investigation of tote addition/removal correctness.
